items.item: No generated face, avatar or synthetic human in any frame
items.note: Thirty-six frames, one every ten seconds. Kinetic cards, the demand-versus-price chart, figure cards, one chapter card and the corner mark; no figure, no avatar, nothing photographic anywhere in the film.
No texture is used at all. Every frame is the paper room: type, the chart, or the chapter card's hairline and title (f-020).

items.item: Every number on screen traces to a model run, and demo data is labelled
items.note: Every figure comes from facts.json and run.json through the reveal loop; nothing is typed into a scene. ELASTICITY.FIT, PRICE.OPTIMUM and MARGIN.DECOMP on Tarnhollow demo data, seed 42. The TARNHOLLOW DEMO DATA chip is on every frame but the chapter card (f-020), which carries no figure.

items.item: Charts are Manim scenes driven by engine output, not hand-rebuilt
items.note: scenes/charts.py Elasticity, reading run.json's elasticity_curves for the SKU named in facts.json: the monthly points, the fitted curve and the interval band are all the model's own arrays. The callout column and the two inline annotations are the reveal loop reading facts.json.

items.item: Every chart builds progressively and carries an annotation
items.note: Caught in the frames this time: axes and their numbers alone with the first points at f-006, then the band and the fitted line at f-007, then the slope annotation ε = -2.20 at f-010, then the interval annotation above the band with the band deepening behind it at f-011. Each landing takes a data tick.

items.item: Room tone, data ticks, transition SFX and a ducking bed
items.note: mix.json carries the locked sound: room tone at -48 dB, the ticks and whooshes from ElevenLabs sound generation, bed-elevenlabs.mp3 at -32 dB ducking to -20 dB. qa.json reads no silence over a second and -16.9 LUFS against a -16 target.

items.item: A publishable voice, disclosed as what it is
items.note: voice is "library": the ElevenLabs library voice the founder chose on 2026-10-04 (content/assets/voice.json), which PREMIUM-STANDARD accepts as amended. The description does not exist yet, so qa.json reports disclosure_in_description as null; that is the describe step's check.

items.item: Cut to VISUAL_SPEC §4, and nothing frozen over four seconds
items.note: qa.json: 39 cuts, mean interval 9.06 s, longest 28.5 s, inside the thirty a chart build may hold, and the frames show something new landing inside it every few seconds (the callout pair turns over at f-023, f-024, f-025, f-026, f-027, f-028). No frozen run anywhere, max_hold 0.0 s.

items.item: Subtitles burned in, legible, never boxed
items.note: Coverage 1.0, transcript match 0.982, the best of the three units cut so far. Inter Display in ink with a thin paper outline, two lines, centred over a wide bottom margin; no box. The chart keeps out of the band on every frame.

items.item: The style lock is written and followed
items.note: content/assets/style-lock.json, locked from V01 on 2026-10-05. Paper, ink, one blue, Inter Display at the stage's sizes; the chapter card at f-020 is the spec's hairline and title. Nothing in these frames departs from it.

items.item: One blue element per frame, and blue only on money and the leak
items.note: Blue falls on the fit's interval band and on the spoken money figures ($3.5M at f-007, $1,701 at f-028). VISUAL_SPEC §8.4 names the band as the one thing besides money that takes blue, so the band is right. The two-places question stands exactly as V04 and V05 left it: a frame carrying a blue money callout beside the blue band (f-007, f-009, f-028) has blue twice, which the house grammar allows but only the founder can settle for the series. No red and no green anywhere.

items.item: No gradient, glow, halo or vignette; hard cuts only
items.note: None in any frame. Transitions are hard cuts; the only motion inside a shot is the drift the spec asks for.

items.item: At most three text blocks per frame, captions small and dim
items.note: The busiest frames are the chart ones: heading, the interval annotation on the band, and at most two callouts in the right column, with the burned-in subtitle counted separately. The annotation replaces itself rather than stacking, which is the V04 fix working (charts.py:354-370).

items.item: Charts have direct labels, a demo label, no legend and no grid
items.note: Hairline axes with two numbers on each, the slope named on the curve, the interval named on the band, the demo chip bottom left. No legend and no gridlines anywhere.

Every placeholder in this script survives its substitution: the values that carry no unit are the ones whose sentences supply it ("wait 5 months" at f-031, "moved by 2% across 5 months" at f-025), and the ones that carry a unit are never given a second ("-2.20", "32.1% of revenue", "a 5.0% step to $37.84", "a 4% chance it loses money"). Nothing here repeats V05's and V07's double unit.

items.item: The narration describes the picture that is actually on screen
items.note: Three things, and the first is the real one. (1) The whole middle of the film is about a shape the viewer never sees. CHAPTER 1 says "as the price climbs, profit climbs, then flattens, then falls. It's a hill. Every product has one. The top of the hill is the price you want", and CHAPTER 2 says "the top isn't a point ... the top is a stretch of hill". The script's VISUAL lines ask for exactly that: the profit hill built underneath the demand line, a second lower hill drawn off the gross margin to show the wrong top, then the top shaded into a stretch. charts.py has no hill scene — Waterfall, CashCone, Paths, Elasticity, Newsvendor, SampleSize and nothing else — so both beats fall back to Elasticity, and for two and a half minutes the narration describes a hill over a straight fitted line (f-012 to f-019, f-021 to f-028). The argument of the video is the hill; it is the one picture the film does not have. (2) The chapter-2 chart is a leftover: it holds TH-OVEMIT-22's scatter and its "-0.88 · upper bound of its ninety-five percent interval" annotation while the narration has moved to the catalogue's counts and to TH-CASIRO-01's step (f-023 to f-028), so the picture names one SKU while the voice names another. (3) THUMBNAIL on script.md line 2 asks for "{{el_point}} in amber over the elasticity fragment"; amber is retired by VISUAL_SPEC §3.1 (2026-10-04) and the film carries no amber pixel, the same leftover found in V05 and V07.

notes: Sixteen items, fifteen passing. The render is clean on every mechanical count — the cadence, the frozen-picture check, the mix, the subtitles at 0.982 against the script, the palette, the type — and the number safety is clean, which is what V05 and V07 were blocked on. What fails is the picture itself: the film argues the profit hill and never draws it, because the scene does not exist yet. That is build work on this branch, not a founder decision, and it is the next thing this unit needs: a Hill scene in scenes/charts.py driven by PRICE.OPTIMUM's own curve, drawing the profit hill under the demand line, the second hill off the gross margin, and the top as a shaded stretch at the interval, plus a catalogue picture for chapter 2 so the chart stops naming a SKU the narration has left. The one thing only the founder can give is the third correction: take "in amber" out of the thumbnail line of the approved script. The step is blocked on that, and on the Hill scene landing before the unit re-renders from scenes.
